title: scenario-driven-customer-briefcase-2026
author: Jordan Lee
content:
Summary:

This briefcase is a scenario-driven sales kit designed for pre-sales conversations with platform and infrastructure leaders (CTO/Head of Platform) evaluating inference architectures. It bundles: concise positioning, a competitive comparison matrix, three customer scenarios with suggested pricing anchors, an exemplar one‑slide pitch, an abbreviated security FAQ for technical reviewers, and a short results-focused case study. Use as a compact, reproducible artifact in demos, field calls, and technical deep dives.

Contents (quick navigation):
1) Leading positioning statements
2) Competitive snapshot (matrix)
3) Three realistic customer scenarios + pricing anchors
4) Single-slide pitch script and structure
5) Security & procurement FAQ (short answers)
6) Compact case study: Nimbus Retail
7) Action checklist and owner assignments

1) Leading positioning statements

- One-line elevator: "Deliver predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, reserved, and private deployments so your product teams avoid costly rework and unpredictable unit economics."
- For CTOs: Emphasize measurable operational levers: latency SLOs, per‑token USD economics, and deterministic fallbacks (model variant routing).
- For Platform Leads: Emphasize a single API, observable model-level telemetry, and rollout controls that integrate with existing CI/CD.
- For Security/Compliance: Emphasize VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit-grade logs + exportable evidence.

Positioning bullets to use in calls:
- "Run the same inference contract in public, dedicated or fully private environments without code changes."
- "We trade upfront model-wrangling for runtime automation—intelligent batching, KV prefix cache and quantization profiles that reduce token costs by 30–60% on common workloads."
- "When capacity or region issues arise, automated policy routing downgrades gracefully to compatible variants to meet SLAs."

2) Competitive snapshot (matrix)

Explanation: Use this 3-way matrix to quickly position Redwood against common alternatives.

Competitor types: Cloud Managed Endpoints (big cloud providers), LLM API Providers (simplicity-first), Self-hosted Inference Runtimes (engineering-first).

Comparison table (short):

| Dimension                        | Redwood Inference                    | Cloud Managed Endpoints              | Self-hosted Runtimes                 |
|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Deployment Modes                | Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC)   | Hosted                               | Private only                         |
| Predictable Unit Economics     | Optimized with batching + caching    | Variable, often higher at scale      | Controlled but requires ops overhead  |
| Observability & Tooling        | Token-level, per-model dashboards    | Basic metrics                        | Varies (team builds instrumentation)  |
| Rollout & Fallbacks            | Canary/A-B + automatic fallbacks     | Limited                              | Custom solutions required             |
| Compliance & Private Deploy    | Private control plane + KMS/HSM      | Strong (but multi-tenant)            | Strong (but heavy integration)        |
| Time to Prod (typical)         | Days – weeks (self-serve -> dedicated)| Days – weeks                         | Weeks – months                        |

How to use:
- If prospect already on cloud managed endpoints: emphasize cost predictability and fallback routing to avoid throttling during peaks.
- If prospect leaning self-hosted: emphasize Redwood reduces engineering lift and accelerates guardrailed rollouts.

3) Three customer scenarios + pricing anchors

Scenario A — High-throughput conversational SaaS (PLG):
- Profile: Multi-tenant product with bursts, ~400 qps peak per region, median seq len 64 tokens, sensitive to 99th percentile latency.
- Suggested deployment: Dedicated capacity with autoscale and burst pool. Enable prefix caching and 8-bit quantization.
- Pricing anchor (example): Dedicated commit: $18,000/month for baseline pod group (supports ~120 sustained qps); incremental burst units billed at $0.22 per 1k tokens; projected unit cost reduction vs cloud-managed baseline: ~45% for typical prompt mixes.
- Sales hooks: emphasize predictable commit price, SLA for 99th p95 latency, and per-route cost dashboards.

Scenario B — Regulated enterprise (financial services):
- Profile: On‑prem or VPC-only, strict audit and key control, data residency in EU.
- Suggested deployment: Private (customer-managed VPC) with Redwood control plane in region, KMS/HSM integration, 12‑month enterprise licensing + support.
- Pricing anchor (example): Platform license $85k/year + per-GPU support/ops fee $2,400/month per GPU; professional services: 6 weeks integration at $40k.
- Sales hooks: compliance pack, SOC2 artifacts, SAML/SCIM and audit log exports.

Scenario C — R&D / Proof-of-Concept (low commitment):
- Profile: Team experimenting with embeddings and reranking for search, low qps but variable seq lengths.
- Suggested deployment: Hosted API, pay-as-you-go, pre-configured quantization suggestions for embeddings, and shared sandbox.
- Pricing anchor (example): Hosted rate: $0.006 per 1k embedding units, $0.035 per 1k generation tokens for opt-weighted models; free trial credits for 30 days.
- Sales hooks: quick onboarding, usage dashboards, and a clear migration path to Dedicated if needed.

4) One-slide pitch structure (30–90 seconds)

Title (5–10s): "Inference you can rely on in production"
Problem (10–15s): "Teams face unpredictable unit costs, flaky latency at scale, and brittle rollouts across environments."
Solution (20–30s): "Redwood provides a single inference contract across hosted, dedicated and private environments — with automatic batching, KV caching, and deterministic fallback policies that preserve SLA and reduce token costs."
Evidence (10–15s): "Customers see 30–60% unit cost reductions on typical generation workloads and deterministic failover across regions."
Call to action (5–10s): "Run a 4‑week bounded POC: we’ll set a dedicated pool, collect metrics, and produce a cost/latency delta report."

Speaker notes (short):
- Start with the customer scenario most similar to the prospect (pick A/B/C).
- Repeat the measurable outcomes (percent cost reduction, SLO numbers).
- Close by offering a concrete next step: "I’ll send a 4‑week POC plan and the measurement dashboard template."

5) Security & procurement FAQ (short answers for technical reviewers)

Q: How are customer inputs and outputs protected?
A: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. For Private deployments, keys may be customer-managed via KMS or HSM. All request/response payloads can be redacted from logs on a per‑route basis.

Q: Do you provide SOC2 / ISO / penetration test evidence?
A: Yes — SOC2 Type II report available under NDA. Annual penetration testing reports and vulnerability scans are available for enterprise procurement packages.

Q: How do you support data residency and export controls?
A: Deployments can be scoped to region (hosted region selection) and Private deployments run fully inside customer VPC. We provide retention controls and automated exportable audit logs (JSON) for compliance.

Q: What access control integrations exist?
A: SAML/SCIM for SSO and provisioning, RBAC at token and route levels, IP allowlists, and optional short‑lived credentials for ephemeral workloads.

Q: How do you ensure model lineage and evidence for audits?
A: Every model version is tracked with immutable metadata: checksum, quantization profile used, kernel selection hints, and the rollout window. We can export model-versioned inference logs linked to request IDs for audit chains.

Q: What is the incident response SLA?
A: For Dedicated customers on enterprise SLAs: page within 15 minutes, 24/7 escalation, and a post‑incident report within 72 hours.

6) Compact case study: Nimbus Retail (abstracted)

Context:
- Customer: Omni-channel retail product team shipping smart search and summary features in their app.
- Challenge: Seasonality-driven traffic spikes overloaded existing endpoint-based model hosting; costs ballooned and 99th percentile latency spiked to 1.8s on peak.

Approach:
1) Deployed Redwood Dedicated pool in primary region with autoscale + burst pool.
2) Enabled KV prefix caching for 70% of queries; applied recommended quantization profile for the target model.
3) Rolled out conservative canary (5% traffic) with automatic fallback policy to a smaller variant when latency risk exceeded thresholds.

Results (30-day rolling window):
- 99th percentile latency reduced from 1.8s -> 0.45s.
- Average inference token cost reduced by 48%.
- User-perceived errors due to timeouts fell 86%.
- Migration time from POC to production: 3 weeks.

Testimonial (paraphrased): "Redwood gave us a reliable path to keep features live during holiday peaks without hiring more infra engineers." — Head of Platform, Nimbus Retail

7) Action checklist and owner assignments

- Pre-call prep (AE+SE): pick scenario A/B/C that matches prospect and prepare the corresponding pricing anchor (owner: AE).
- Technical review packet (SE): attach SOC2 NDA, region/tenant configuration doc, and model-versioning evidence template (owner: SE).
- POC plan template: 4-week measurable plan with success criteria: p50/p95 latency, per-token unit costs, and error rate (owner: Solutions Eng).
- Legal & procurement: attach Enterprise Licensing outline for Private (owner: legal).

|----------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------------------------|-------|

| Token cost per 1k tokens   | $0.60                         | <= $0.35                           | Finance/Sales |
| Error rate (timeouts)      | 1.6%                          | <= 0.3%                            | SE    |
| Model-variant fallback hit | 0%                            | <= 1% (expected)                   | Infra |
